Snow has a way of simplifying the world, the way grief simplifies a life. It erases the ornamental, the decorative, the unnecessary, and leaves behind only the essential geometries: the line of a rooftop, the curve of a road, the sharp vertical of a chimney exhaling smoke into a colorless sky. She watched it fall from behind the kitchen window, her coffee cooling in her hands. Each flake was a small act of erasure... covering the yard, the garden, the path where he used to walk the dog. The dog was gone now too. Not dead, just elsewhere. Like so many things. The snow accumulated with the patience of someone who knows they will win eventually. By noon, the world outside was featureless, a blank page waiting for a sentence she did not yet know how to write. She put on her boots. She opened the door. She stepped into the whiteness and left the first marks, her footprints like punctuation in an unfinished story.
